I have a feeling that it needs to have long engaged to perform best, but I'm not sure if that's the case. It might be very affected by lighting conditions. It got better when it got darker. This actually has been my exact experience. The old models don’t work well with NNLC but the TR models seem better with it. 

That being said I need to collect logs to train a better model for my car. Do you know if we can use the old logs that openpilot has for each car and just supplement them with our own? It does well most of the time just high speed is lacking.
I would collect your own logs from scratch. Try to avoid helping the steering wheel while it steers for you. Less human torque means cleaner data for training.
Will do, I mostly have high speed highway at the edge of torque limits so that will work well. Does the model used matter for training? New vs old sim?

Use whatever settings is the most correct for now if it will help you avoid the need for human torque inputs. If you need to take over do so deliberately. Don't "help it" steer just a little bit. That's the type it might fail to detect the difference between human or not.
I can use MADS to adjust speed to keep steering online for the whole highway drive. I’m assuming that works. Unless that counts as intervention
That's perfect.
That's recommended by the legendary author of NNLC himself.

2017 Hyuandai Ioniq 28kw -  Just had a quite impressive drive with this model. No NNLC. Drove like a champ on country roads with not the best lane markings. My best experience so far with OP/SP. The only thing lacking was weak steering in sharp-ish turns. Don't know if that possible to fix. Anyway, this is my goto model atm.
Also: don’t know if it’s a quirk of my car or the model. But it handles sharp right hand turns better than left hand ones.
